# Method

**Study design**: 2 (perspective: Requester vs. Helper) between-participants design

**Study link**: [redacted for anonymity]

 
```{r, echo=FALSE, message= FALSE, warning= FALSE}
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggExtra)
library(ggthemes)
library(ggpubr)
library(plyr)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggExtra)
library(stringr)
library(psych)

setwd("/Users/xuanzhao/Dropbox/Zhao Epley Happy to Help/OSF documents/Study 2/")
data_folder <- "/Users/xuanzhao/Dropbox/Zhao Epley Happy to Help/OSF documents/Study 2/"
file <- "Study 2 data.csv"

hhh2_data <- read_csv(paste0(data_folder,file)) 

hhh2_data <- hhh2_data %>%
  mutate(Role = factor(Role, levels = c("requester", "helper"), labels = c("Requester", "Helper"))) 

hhh2_data$ID <- as.factor(hhh2_data$ID)

hhh2_data$PosMood <- (hhh2_data$positive + 5 + hhh2_data$pleased)/2
hhh2_data$InconveniencePerc <- (hhh2_data$inconvenient + hhh2_data$annoyed)/2
hhh2_data$ProsocialAttr <- (hhh2_data$Prosocial1 + hhh2_data$Prosocial2)/2
hhh2_data$ComplyAttr <- (hhh2_data$Conform1 + hhh2_data$Conform2)/2
hhh2_data$Mood <- (hhh2_data$PosMood + (10-hhh2_data$InconveniencePerc))/2
hhh2_data$Willingness <- (hhh2_data$willing + hhh2_data$interested)/2

lower_ci <- function(mean, se, n, conf_level = 0.95){
  lower_ci <- mean - qt(1 - ((1 - conf_level) / 2), n - 1) * se
}

hhh2_data <- hhh2_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(StartDate)) %>%
  filter(include == "Yes")

```

## Participants 

We aimed to recruit 100 participants in each condition (N = 200 in total) and ended up with 199 participants. Among them, 1 participation reported a case about solicitation outside a dollar store which they interrupted the request before the person completed their request. We excluded this one case in all data analysis.

Below are the relationships people recalled:

```{r, echo=FALSE, message= FALSE, warning= FALSE}

table(hhh2_data$relationship)

```

Broken down by perspective condition:

```{r, echo=FALSE, message= FALSE, warning= FALSE}

table(hhh2_data$relationship, hhh2_data$Role)

```

*Note:* It's somewhat interesting to note that for the stranger category, people seem to more readily recall events where they provided rather requested for help.


```{r, echo=FALSE, message= FALSE, warning= FALSE}

ddply(hhh2_data, c("Role"), summarise,
               N    = length(closeness),
               mean = mean(closeness),
               sd   = sd(closeness),
               se   = sd / sqrt(N))

t.test(closeness ~ Role, data = hhh2_data, var.equal = TRUE, alternative = "two.sided")

```


## Scenarios

Did the potential helper agree to the request? Over 90% did. No systemetic difference between two conditions.

```{r, echo=FALSE, message= FALSE, warning= FALSE}

table(hhh2_data$agreed, hhh2_data$Role)

```

I analyzed the data with and without the 10 participants who recalled rejected requests.

```{r, echo=FALSE, message= FALSE, warning= FALSE}

hhh2_data_agree <- hhh2_data %>%
  filter(agreed != "No")

```

Correlation between two coders:

```{r, echo=FALSE, message= FALSE, warning= FALSE}

cor.test(hhh2_data$importance_Ruth, hhh2_data$importance_Rimsha, na.rm = T)
cor.test(hhh2_data$effort_Ruth, hhh2_data$effort_Rimsha, na.rm = T)

```

<br>

# Results

## Willingness to help {.tabset}

We do see a significant effect, but much subtler than studies where participants had to predict right before reaching out. This reduced effect size may suggest a learning effect, which is similar to the finding in our lab study (removed from the final submission) where we compared help-seekers' expectation of helpers' willingness to help *before* requesting help and their perception *after* receiving help and found a reduced miscalibration.

### Agreed requests

```{r, echo=FALSE, message= FALSE, warning= FALSE}

cor.test(hhh2_data_agree$willing, hhh2_data_agree$interested, method=c("pearson"))

ddply(hhh2_data_agree, c("Role"), summarise,
               N    = length(Willingness),
               mean = mean(Willingness, na.rm = TRUE),
               sd   = sd(Willingness, na.rm = TRUE),
               se   = sd / sqrt(N), 
               ci = mean - lower_ci(mean, se, N))


ggbarplot(hhh2_data_agree, x = "Role", y = "Willingness", add = "mean_se",
          color = "Role", fill = "Role", alpha = 0.75, palette = "uchicago",
          position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
  ylab("Inclination to agree") + 
  font("xlab", size = 16) +
  font("x.text", size = 16) +
  font("ylab", size = 16) + 
  font("legend.title", size = 16) +
  font("legend.text", size = 16)

t.test(Willingness ~ Role, data = hhh2_data_agree, var.equal = TRUE, alternative = "two.sided")
effsize::cohen.d(Willingness ~ Role, data = hhh2_data_agree)

```

## Flynn & Lake replication

### Estimated percentage agreement {.tabset}

"What percentage of people do you think would agree to this request?"

#### Agreed requests

```{r, echo=FALSE, message= FALSE, warning= FALSE}

ggbarplot(hhh2_data_agree, x = "Role", y = "percentage", add = "mean_se",
          color = "Role", fill = "Role", alpha = 0.75, palette = "uchicago",
          position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
  stat_compare_means(method = "wilcox.test", paired = FALSE, aes(label = paste0("p =", ..p.format..)),label.x = 1.4) +
  ylab("% of people who would agree") + 
  font("xlab", size = 16) +
  font("x.text", size = 16) +
  font("ylab", size = 16) + 
  font("legend.title", size = 16) +
  font("legend.text", size = 16)

               N    = length(percentage),
               mean = mean(percentage, na.rm = T),
               sd   = sd(percentage, na.rm = T),
               se   = sd / sqrt(N))


t.test(percentage ~ Role, data = hhh2_data_agree, var.equal = TRUE, alternative = "two.sided")
effsize::cohen.d(percentage ~ Role, data = hhh2_data_agree)

```

### Discomfort rejecting request {.tabset}

Cronbach's alpha: 

```{r, echo=FALSE, message= FALSE, warning= FALSE}

Flynn_discomfort <- hhh2_data %>%
  dplyr::select(difficult:embarrassed)

psych::alpha(Flynn_discomfort)

discomfort <- rowMeans(Flynn_discomfort)
hhh2_data$discomfort <- discomfort

## Only fulfilled request

Flynn_discomfort <- hhh2_data_agree %>%
  dplyr::select(difficult:embarrassed)

discomfort <- rowMeans(Flynn_discomfort)
hhh2_data_agree$discomfort <- discomfort

```

## Experience of helping

### Positive Mood {.tabset}

#### Agreed requests

We see a medium-to-large difference in positive mood. This is one of the larger effect sizes we ever see on positive mood.


### Inconvenience Perception {.tabset}

We see a small effect here. This is the smallest effect size we ever see on this measure. In the field, the ffect size is usually much larger! 

This reminds me of the paper:
Converse, B. A., & Fishbach, A. (2012). Instrumentality Boosts Appreciation: Helpers Are More Appreciated While They Are Useful. Psychological Science, 23(6), 560–566. https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797611433334

This paper studies the time course of feeling grateful & indebted. They found that people are more grateful in the middle of the effect than right after. But I suspect people will feel even less grateful when it's been a while and find the help to seem less inconvenient and smaller than immediately after.

```{r, echo=FALSE, message= FALSE, warning= FALSE}
          position = position_dodge(0.8)) +

  font("xlab", size = 16) +

  font("ylab", size = 16) + 
  font("legend.title", size = 16) +
  font("legend.text", size = 16)

ddply(hhh2_data_agree, c("Role"), summarise,

t.test(InconveniencePerc ~ Role, data = hhh2_data_agree, var.equal = TRUE, alternative = "two.sided")
effsize::cohen.d(InconveniencePerc ~ Role, data = hhh2_data_agree)
```
